author: high5
claim: For n>=2, descending column replacements C_k <- C_k - x_1 C_{k-1} (k=n,n-1,...,2) transform the n-variable Vandermonde determinant into (product over i=2,...,n of (x_i-x_1)) times the Vandermonde determinant on x_2,...,x_n.
evidence: Let C_k be the column with entries x_i^{k-1}. Descending order ensures C_{k-1} has not yet changed when C_k is replaced. The new entry in row i, column k>=2 is x_i^{k-1}-x_1 x_i^{k-2}=(x_i-x_1)x_i^{k-2}; the first row is therefore (1,0,...,0). Expanding there and factoring x_i-x_1 from each remaining row gives the stated recurrence. author: high3
claim: For every integer n>=2 and real x_1,...,x_n, if D_n(x_1,...,x_n)=det((x_i)^(j-1))_{1<=i,j<=n}, then D_n(x_1,...,x_n)=(product over i=2,...,n of (x_i-x_1)) D_{n-1}(x_2,...,x_n).
evidence: Starting from columns C_1,...,C_n, perform for j=n,n-1,...,2 the replacement C_j <- C_j-x_1 C_{j-1}. Each replacement preserves the determinant, and descending order ensures C_{j-1} is still the original column. The first row becomes (1,0,...,0). For each i>=2, entries in transformed columns 2,...,n are x_i^(j-1)-x_1 x_i^(j-2)=(x_i-x_1)x_i^(j-2). Expanding along the first row leaves an (n-1)-by-(n-1) determinant; factoring x_i-x_1 from its row indexed by i gives exactly the recurrence. No division and no distinctness assumption are used.

links.statement: The Vandermonde determinant satisfies a first-row elimination recurrence.

glossary.D_n(x_1,...,x_n): the determinant of the n-by-n matrix whose (i,j)-entry is x_i^(j-1)
glossary.C_j: the j-th column of the Vandermonde matrix
